newsitem.title: GERMANY: Waigel to discuss Buba gold for budget, not sales.
newsitem.headline: Waigel to discuss Buba gold for budget, not sales.

text.p: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel plans to discuss revaluing Germany's gold reserves with the Bundesbank but not selling them, government coalition sources said on Thursday.

The sources said Waigel, who was due to take part in a Bundesbank council meeting on Thursday in Frankfurt, was considering a revaluation that would lead to a higher figure for the annual profit the bank turns over to the government.
A finance ministry spokeswoman had earlier denied press reports that Bonn planned to sell Bundesbank gold to free up more funds to fill new gaping holes in its budget deficit.

In its Thursday edition, the Handelsblatt newspaper wrote that revaluing Bundesbank gold reserves could help free up hidden reserves. It said the Bundesbank currently holds 95 million ounces of gold which it has valued at 13.7 billion marks while the market value is seen at 57 billion marks.
The Bundesbank declined to comment on the report.
